facts.fact: The health ministry's RASS 2020 describes the reporting chain: first-contact establishments (ESPC), general hospitals and regional hospital centres each draw up a monthly activity report from the registers care providers fill in, the reports go to the departmental health directorate, and there the district's epidemiological surveillance officer keys all the data of the reports received from the ESPC into the DHIS2 database.

The RASS 2020, by the ministry's DIIS, puts national completeness of entry of the monthly SIG activity report forms in DHIS2 at 100% for 2020, against 99.3% in 2019 and a national target of 95%, with every health region at 100%, and timeliness of entry at 98.23%, against 88.1% in 2019 and a target of 80%.

By the RASS 2020's account of data collection, the first-contact establishments (ESPC) do not enter their own reports: all the data of the monthly reports received from the ESPC are keyed into DHIS2 at the departmental health directorate by the district's epidemiological surveillance officer.

The RASS 2020 states that the data of the referral hospitals, the general hospitals and regional hospital centres, are keyed into DHIS2 by the hospitals' own data managers, while the reports of first-contact establishments are keyed at the departmental health directorate.

The RASS 2020 calls DHIS2 the national database of routine data from public, faith-based and NGO health establishments and places its checking with the health ministry: regional surveillance officers verify completeness, timeliness and consistency, and the Cellule d'Appui Technique au Système d'Informations Sanitaires (CATSIS), housed in the ministry's Direction de l'Informatique et de l'Information Sanitaire, verifies completeness and timeliness nationally.

systems.country_label: base de données nationale DHIS2, taking the monthly reports of the SIG (Système d'Information et de Gestion)
systems.owner: Ministry of health (MSHPCMU), Direction de l'Informatique et de l'Information Sanitaire (DIIS), through its CATSIS unit
systems.tiers: keyed at the departmental health directorates for first-contact establishments (ESPC) and by the data managers of general hospitals and regional hospital centres; checked at regional and national level; the report notes weak integration of private, community and other ministries' data
